record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs are rectangle visibility graphs, where vertices are isothetic rectangles with pairwise disjoint interiors and two vertices are adjacent exactly when their rectangles are horizontally or vertically visible by an unobstructed beam of finite width.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 27 Characterize rectangle visibility graphs.

artifact.status_search_result: No complete combinatorial characterization of rectangle visibility graphs is known. Recognition of rectangle visibility graphs is NP-hard, and known results are limited to partial classes (e.g., bounds on edge counts, results on unit rectangle visibility graphs, and polynomial-time recognition only for specialized variants such as topological rectangle visibility graphs). The general characterization remains an open problem.
